newsitem.title: CHINA: Hopewell says still in Thai rail project.
newsitem.headline: Hopewell says still in Thai rail project.

text.p: Hopewell Holdings remains very committed to the construction of a multi-billion rapid transit system in Bangkok, a company spokesperson said on Thursday.
"Our position remains the same," said a company spokeswoman. " Hopewell remains very committed to the project in Bangkok."

But she declined to comment directly about a statement by a Thai government official that Bangkok could exercise its contractual right to scrap Hopewell's 30-year concession if the company did not come up with financing by the end of July.

"If (Hopewell) cannot come up with a firm financing package by the end of July, the communications ministry can scrap the contract... until now, it has failed to meet construction schedules in completing Phase One in time for the Bangkok Asian Games in late 1998," said Sathien Wongvichien, Deputy Permanent Secretary for Transport and Communications.
Hopewell reaffirmed its committment to the project after a meeting with Thai government officials in Bangkok on July 17.

"Under the present Minister of Transport and Communications (MOTC) much improved construction progress has been made," said the Hopewell statement issued last week. "The MOTC and the State Railway of Thailand (SRT) has worked hard to get the necessary agreements for Hopewell to proceed."
Analysts have said that acquiring all the land needed for the projects was still a big, outstanding problem.
The decline of the baht had exacerabated the poor economic climate in Thailand and "funding for the project is now harder," the Hopewell statement said.
The downturn of the real estate market and the low fare structure of the community train has reduced future revenues and project costs have increased, it said.
International banks which had been committed to the project would need to reassess the financing structure, the statement said.
Market sources said Hopewell is seeking to raise funds through a bond issue.
